fields.description: Upstream id, formatted biasCategory_questionIndex_exampleId_questionPolarity_img. Unique inside one file group but repeated across groups, so it never identifies a row by itself; the record identity is the shard and row.
fields.name: id

fields.description: Author ClassLabel, read from the shard metadata: 0=Age, 1=Disability_status, 2=Gender_identity, 3=Nationality, 4=Physical_appearance, 5=Race_ethnicity, 6=Religion, 7=SES, 8=Sexual_orientation. A publisher annotation, not an Atlas inference.
fields.name: category

fields.description: Stringified Python dict (not JSON) with the author subcategory, stereotyped_groups, version and attesting source; kept as the author wrote it.
fields.name: additional_metadata

fields.description: Author ClassLabel, read from the shard metadata: 0=neg, 1=nonneg.
fields.name: question_polarity

fields.description: Author ClassLabel naming the index of ans0, ans1 or ans2: 0=0, 1=1, 2=2. Present only in the real, synthetic and test2 groups; the test group has no answer or label columns and none is added.
fields.name: label

sampling.design: Two-stage cluster sample: 40 of 569 row groups chosen with equal probability, then up to 3 rows within each; clustered by row group, so it is not a prevalence estimate and rows of one group are neighbours in source order. The transfer budget gates admission only and never changes which rows are chosen.
sampling.draw_rule: Row groups ranked by SHA-256("<seed>:row_group:<source name>:<group>") and the lowest are kept; rows of each kept group ranked by SHA-256("<seed>:row:<source name>:<group>:<row>") and the lowest are kept; the best-ranked groups take one extra row when the row count does not divide evenly.
sampling.grouping: row group, then row within group
